subject: Private deployment observability: ingest endpoints and SIEM handoff
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@acmebank.com>, Acme Bank Security Team <security@acmebank.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop, vivek_kulkarni, stephanie_nguyen
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment observability: ingest endpoints and SIEM handoff

Hi Marta / Acme Sec team —

Thanks for the time last week. As we prep the on-prem/VPC handoff for the Redwood Private deployment, we want to lock down the observability export plan so we don't hit any compliance surprises during onboarding. Key items we need clarity on from your side: 

- Primary collectors you accept (Splunk HEC, QRadar, Elastic, in-house)
- Preferred transport format (CEF, JSON, HEC token) and TLS / mTLS requirements
- Allowed egress model: static egress IP range, NAT gateway, PrivateLink/VPN allowed?
- Retention/PII rules for logs and traces (especially input prompts/utterances)
- Tracing propagation headers you require (W3C traceparent, b3, custom)

Attached is a short adapter spec and a proposed network flow diagram for a small forwarder running inside the customer VPC (redwood_onprem_obsv_adapter_v1.pdf, network_flow_diagram.png). We can support:

- Direct HEC push over TLS (client certs optional)
- A local Unix socket forwarder that writes to Splunk/HEC to minimize egress
- Structured JSON events for traces/metrics with optional token redaction hooks

Ask: can you confirm the collector(s) and whether your security team requires mutual TLS or client certs for HEC? Also, please point me to the onboarding checklist and any network allowlists so we can draft a clean runbook.

Proposed next step: 30–45m technical sync this week with your Sec+Infra and our SEs to finalize the ingest pattern.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_onprem_obsv_adapter_v1.pdf, network_flow_diagram.png
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@acmebank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Bank Security Team <security@acmebank.com>, lauren_bishop, vivek_kulkarni
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment observability: ingest endpoints and SIEM handoff

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the doc. A few clarifications from Acme Sec: 

- Primary collector: Splunk HEC is preferred. We also have QRadar in a different org; we can connect both but Splunk HEC will be the initial target.
- Format: Splunk HEC JSON (event ~= JSON) is preferred over CEF for telemetry and parsing.
- Auth: we require TLS 1.2+ and mTLS for any direct push to our ingest endpoints. Client certs are mandatory for production.
- Egress: fixed egress IPs are required for allowlisting. PrivateLink is negotiable but we need to assess the network team effort.
- PII: request that any user prompts be redacted or routed to a short-term retention bucket; retention policy is 90 days for raw events, 365 days for parsed metadata.

I've attached our Splunk onboarding checklist (Acme_Splunk_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf) and copied Tim O'Hara from our integration vendor in case we need third-party forwarder advice.

Can your team provide a small sample (<= 10 events) of the JSON payloads and an example cert rotation process? We need to validate parsing and cert lifecycle with our InfoSec toolkit.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Sr. InfoSec Engineer — Acme Bank

Subject: Re: Private deployment observability: ingest endpoints and SIEM handoff

Thanks Marta — useful constraints. A few concrete implementation notes from our SE side: 

1) Ingest architecture (recommended)
 - Deploy a small Redwood forwarder inside the customer's VPC (single EC2 / small instance) that collects logs/traces locally over a Unix socket from the Redwood runtime.
 - Forwarder batches events and pushes to Splunk HEC over mTLS. We support token-based HEC as backup.
 - Optionally emit a subset of telemetry via PrivateLink to reduce public egress.

2) Payloads
 - We'll send structured JSON with fields: timestamp, service, model_id, trace_id, span_id, event_type, metrics, redaction_flags.
 - Tracing: we support W3C traceparent propagation; we can also inject x-redwood-request-id for debugging.

3) Retention & PII
 - We can configure prompt redaction at the routing layer; raw prompt text can be written to an isolated short-retention bucket (90 days) and parsed metadata retained longer.

4) Cert rotation & keys
 - We recommend rotating client certs every 90 days. Our forwarder supports ACME-like rotation hooks and can integrate with customer KMS/HSM for private key storage.

I've attached an updated network flow with NAT/eip options (network_flow_diagram.png). Next steps: provide 3 sample JSON events and a short runbook for cert rotation. I can produce the samples by EOD.

—Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@acmebank.com>
Cc: jordan_blake, lauren_bishop, stephanie_nguyen
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment observability: ingest endpoints and SIEM handoff

Marta / team —

Appreciate the constraints. A couple of operational items to call out before we lock the design: 

- Egress/IPs: we can provide a small, static egress pool (3 IPs) for allowlisting, or we can terminate via PrivateLink — PrivateLink will require a partner setup and adds ~2 weeks to the network runbook. If Acme accepts the egress pool we can proceed faster.
- High-availability: recommend 2 forwarder instances across AZs with active-active push to Splunk HEC; each forwarder will present its own client certs.
- Fallbacks: if mTLS fails, the forwarder can fall back to token-based HEC and emit a security alert to our ops channel.

I'll prepare the sample egress IPs and a short cert rotation runbook this afternoon. Also linking the internal ticket where we track the PrivateLink option: https://acmebank.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-482

—Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@acmebank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop, vivek_kulkarni, stephanie_nguyen, Acme Bank Security Team <security@acmebank.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment observability: ingest endpoints and SIEM handoff

Jordan / team —

Thanks — this plan looks workable. We approve the Splunk HEC JSON flow with mandatory mTLS for prod and the 90-day rotation cadence you proposed. Acme will accept the static egress IP pool for initial onboarding; please send the three IP addresses and certificate CNs so we can seed the allowlist.

Next steps:
- Redwood: send three sample JSON events and the cert rotation runbook (target: Thu EOD).
- Acme: NetOps to confirm allowlist and create the Splunk ingest token for the RDW forwarder.
- Schedule a 30m kickoff for Friday to validate parsing and ingestion. Please share a calendar invite.

Also, we will need SOC 2 audit evidence for the forwarder code and your SOC2 report in advance of production access — can you attach or link that when you send the samples?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Sr. InfoSec Engineer — Acme Bank

Attachments referenced: Acme_Splunk_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf
